title: The Clockwork Bird
text: A brass bird flits from beam to beam in the ruined forge, singing a song from the forge's best days, when the furnaces roared and the smiths were proud. Its wings click. Its song is slowing, each note a little lower than the last. It is running down.

options.label: The cleverest hands wind it up again, so that its song may go on.

outcomes.text: It sings, brighter, and leads you through the ruins to its maker's room, where it has been waiting to go.

options.label: Catch it for the House. A thing so fine should not be left to rust.

outcomes.text: It is a fine toy, and worth a lot, and it never stops trying to escape.
Its beak is sharp, and brass, and it goes for the eyes, and does not like being caught.

options.label: Let it run down. Its maker is long gone, and so are its best days.

outcomes.text: The song slows, and slows, and stops mid-note, and the forge is very quiet, and very dead.
